subject: social
source: NCERT Democratic Politics II (Class X Political Science), Chapter 3

questions.q: When we speak of gender divisions, we usually refer to…
questions.a: unequal roles assigned by society to men and women
w: biological differences between men and women
absence of voting rights for women
questions.e: Gender division is based on social expectations and stereotypes, not biology.

questions.q: A system in which all work inside the home is done or organised by the women of the family is called…
questions.a: sexual division of labour
questions.e: Men do outside work; women’s household work is unpaid and unrecognised.

questions.q: A woman or man who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men is called a…
questions.a: feminist
questions.e: Radical women’s movements aiming at equality in personal and family life are feminist movements.

questions.q: Patriarchy literally means…
questions.a: rule by father – a system that values men more and gives them power over women
w: rule by elders of a caste
questions.e: India is still a male-dominated, patriarchal society.

questions.q: Which Act provides that equal wages should be paid for equal work?
questions.a: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976
questions.e: Yet in many areas women are still paid less than men.

questions.q: In which countries is the participation of women in public life very high?
questions.a: Scandinavian countries such as Sweden, Norway and Finland
questions.e: Nordic countries top women’s representation in parliaments.

questions.q: According to the chapter, the literacy rate among women is… compared with … among men.
questions.a: 54 per cent; 76 per cent
questions.e: Fewer girls go for higher studies because parents prefer to spend on boys’ education.

questions.q: The percentage of elected women members in the Lok Sabha touched … for the first time in 2019.
questions.a: 14.36 per cent
questions.e: In State assemblies their share is less than 5 per cent.

questions.q: What does the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women’s Reservation Act), 2023 provide?
questions.a: 33 per cent reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly
questions.e: One-third of seats in panchayats and municipalities were already reserved.

questions.q: The child sex ratio (girls per thousand boys) in India fell to…
questions.e: Due to sex-selective abortion; in some States it fell below 850 or even 800.

questions.q: The time use survey shows that an average Indian woman…
questions.a: works one hour more than an average man each day, but much of her work is unpaid
w: spends no time on household work
questions.e: About 7½ hours for women vs 6½ hours for men.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Gender division should be expressed in politics.
Reason (R): Disadvantaged groups benefit when social divisions become a political issue.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: Women’s gains (voting rights, reservation) came because their unequal treatment was raised politically.

questions.q: Who said that religion can never be separated from politics – meaning moral values that inform all religions?
questions.a: Mahatma Gandhi
questions.e: He believed politics must be guided by ethics drawn from religion.

questions.q: Politics based on the idea that religion is the principal basis of social community is called…
questions.a: communal politics
questions.e: Communalism involves thinking that followers of one religion form one community with the same interests.

questions.q: Which is the most common expression of communalism?
questions.a: Everyday beliefs – religious prejudices and stereotypes
questions.e: Other forms: political dominance, mobilisation on religious lines, communal violence.

questions.q: Which statement about India’s Constitution is WRONG? It…
questions.a: gives official status to one religion
w: prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion
gives freedom to profess any religion
allows the state to ensure equality within religious communities
questions.e: India has no official religion (NCERT exercise 10).

questions.q: Why does the Constitution allow the state to intervene in religious matters?
questions.a: To ensure equality within religious communities – for example, it bans untouchability
questions.e: This is part of India’s model of a secular state.

questions.q: Which statements describe communal politics? A. One religion is superior  B. People of different religions can live together as equal citizens  C. Followers of a religion form one community  D. State power cannot be used for one religion’s domination
questions.a: A and C
questions.e: B and D describe secular ideas (NCERT exercise 9).

questions.q: Unlike India, which country gives a special status to Buddhism?
questions.a: Sri Lanka
questions.e: Islam in Pakistan and Christianity in England also have special status; India has no official religion.

questions.q: According to the 2011 Census, Muslims form about what percentage of India’s population?
questions.a: 14.2 per cent
questions.e: Hindus 79.8%, Muslims 14.2%, Christians 2.3%, Sikhs 1.7%.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Communalism threatens the very idea of India.
Reason (R): Secularism is one of the foundations of our country.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: Because secularism is foundational, communalism attacks the idea of India itself – it is not a threat to only some people.

questions.q: Social divisions based on … are peculiar to India.
questions.a: caste
questions.e: Hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals is special to India.

questions.q: Which reformers worked to establish a society without caste inequalities?
questions.a: Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker
w: Kanshi Ram and Sahu Maharaj only
questions.e: Along with socio-economic changes, their efforts changed the caste system.

questions.q: Shift of population from rural areas to urban areas is called…
questions.a: urbanisation
questions.e: Along with literacy and occupational mobility it weakened old caste hierarchies.

questions.q: According to the 2011 Census, what percentage of India’s population are Scheduled Castes?
questions.a: 16.6 per cent
questions.e: Scheduled Tribes 8.6%; OBCs about 41% (NSS 2004–05).

questions.q: Which is a correct reason why caste alone cannot decide elections in India?
questions.a: No parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one single caste
w: All voters of a caste vote for one party
questions.e: Also: no party gets all votes of a caste, and voters judge performance.

questions.q: Which is an example of ‘politics in caste’ (politics influencing caste)?
questions.a: Caste groups incorporating neighbouring sub-castes to become bigger
w: Parties choosing candidates by caste composition
Appeals to caste sentiment in campaigns
questions.e: Politics changes caste: groups grow, form coalitions and new groups like ‘backward’ and ‘forward’ appear.

questions.q: According to the NSS 1999–2000 data, which group had the highest proportion of rural people below the poverty line?
questions.a: Scheduled Tribes (45.8%)
questions.e: Caste is still strongly linked to economic status.

questions.q: What is a negative effect of politics based only on caste identity?
questions.a: It can divert attention from poverty, development and corruption and lead to tension
w: It gives Dalits access to decision making
It brings new consciousness among lower castes
It forces caste groups to negotiate
questions.e: Caste politics has both positive and negative sides.

questions.q: Match: 1. Believes in equal rights for women and men 2. Religion is the principal basis of community 3. Caste is the principal basis of community 4. Does not discriminate on the basis of religion  with A. Communalist B. Feminist C. Secularist D. Casteist
questions.e: NCERT exercise 12.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Caste has not disappeared from contemporary India.
Reason (R): Most people still marry within their own caste and untouchability has not ended completely.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
w: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.e: R gives the evidence for A.

questions.q: What does the data in the passage show about women in Indian legislatures?
questions.a: Their share is very low – about 14% in Lok Sabha and less than 5% in state assemblies
w: Women hold half the seats in Lok Sabha
Women have one-third reservation in Lok Sabha since 1992
Women are better represented in state assemblies than in Lok Sabha
questions.e: Low representation is why a reservation law for legislatures was demanded.
questions.passage: In India, the proportion of women in legislature has been very low. The percentage of elected women members in Lok Sabha touched 14.36 per cent of its total strength for the first time in 2019. Their share in the state assemblies is less than 5 per cent. One-third of seats in local government bodies – panchayats and municipalities – are now reserved for women. Now there are more than 10 lakh elected women representatives in rural and urban local bodies.

questions.q: How many women representatives are there in rural and urban local bodies?
questions.a: More than 10 lakh
questions.e: One-third reservation in panchayats and municipalities made this possible.
questions.passage: In India, the proportion of women in legislature has been very low. The percentage of elected women members in Lok Sabha touched 14.36 per cent of its total strength for the first time in 2019. Their share in the state assemblies is less than 5 per cent. One-third of seats in local government bodies – panchayats and municipalities – are now reserved for women. Now there are more than 10 lakh elected women representatives in rural and urban local bodies.

questions.q: Which provision in the passage allows the state to act inside religious communities?
questions.a: The state can intervene in religious matters to ensure equality, e.g. banning untouchability
questions.e: Secularism in India is not total separation; the state can intervene for equality.
questions.passage: There is no official religion for the Indian state. Unlike the status of Buddhism in Sri Lanka, that of Islam in Pakistan and that of Christianity in England, our Constitution does not give a special status to any religion. The Constitution provides to all individuals and communities freedom to profess, practice and propagate any religion, or not to follow any. The Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion. At the same time, the Constitution allows the state to intervene in the matters of religion in order to ensure equality within religious communities. For example, it bans untouchability.

questions.q: According to the passage, which country gives a special status to Islam?
questions.a: Pakistan
questions.e: Sri Lanka – Buddhism; Pakistan – Islam; England – Christianity.
